case.title: EVE's Malaysian cell plant
case.subtitle: EVE Energy Malaysia Sdn Bhd · Kulim, Kedah, Malaysia
case.question: Could Sayari show Chinese anode material going into a Chinese-owned battery cell plant in Malaysia, and finished cells coming out to US buyers?
case.answer: Yes. Sayari shows 59 rows of anode graphite from Chinese anode makers going into EVE Energy Malaysia, an ownership chain from the plant to EVE Energy in Huizhou, and 27 rows of cells going to US buyers. What it can't show is which graphite ended up in which cells.
case.why_it_matters: Rerouting at the cell level doesn't need anode material to cross a US border at all. The graphite stays in Malaysia and reaches the US inside a finished cell. For a US company using these cells, the tax-credit question is likely to centre on who made the cell, here a Chinese-owned company that was added to the US Section 1260H list on 8 June 2026, rather than on the graphite inside. We don't make a legal call.
case.headline: Chinese anode material goes in and finished cells come out, and Sayari shows both, plus who owns the plant. EVE Energy Malaysia took 59 rows of anode graphite from seven named suppliers, among them Zhongke, BTR (including BTR's Indonesian plant), Shanshan and Qingdao Taidongrui. It shipped 27 rows of cells to the US for buyers including Briggs & Stratton, Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, TTI and EVE's own US arm. Its owner, EVE Energy, was added to the US 1260H list in June 2026.
case.summary_for_non_experts: EVE Energy is a big Chinese battery maker. In February 2025 it opened its first factory outside China, in Kedah, Malaysia, making small cylindrical cells for power tools and garden equipment. Trade data shows the factory buying graphite anode material, cathode powders and machinery, mostly from China, and selling finished cells to US companies. Registry data links the factory to EVE through a Hong Kong holding company and two shared directors. A second Malaysian plant, Linergy Power, follows the same pattern under a group CATL co-owns.

steps.title: The plant and its owner
steps.text: Malaysian company data names EVE Asia Co., Limited as the plant's only shareholder. Hong Kong registry data shows EVE Energy Co., Ltd. of Huizhou owning 100% of EVE Asia. Two people, Liu Jincheng and Chan Tsun Ming, sit on both boards, and one Malaysian director record gives EVE's own Huizhou street address. EVE's website calls the plant its 53rd factory.

steps.title: Chinese anode material goes in
steps.text: Between Apr 2025 and Apr 2026 the plant received 59 rows of graphite (HS 3801, artificial graphite and graphite preparations) described as 'negative electrode material', 'anode materials' or 'spheroidized graphite'. That is battery grade. Suppliers: Qingdao Taidongrui 19, Zhongke Shinzoom 18 plus 1 from its Guizhou unit, BTR's sales arm 11, BTR's Indonesian plant 5, Shanshan 4 and Hebei Kuntian 1. BTR also sent 4 rows coded as natural flake graphite (HS 2504). EVE's Hong Kong arm co-owns 24% of a BTR company in Changzhou.

steps.title: The rest of the cell comes from China too
steps.text: Of 3,608 inbound rows, 3,285 left from China. Besides graphite, the plant imports HS 2842.90 salts (the code commonly used for cathode powders) from Hunan Yuneng, Hunan Changyuan Lico and Easpring, plus aluminium foil, battery parts, chemicals and machinery. EVE Asia, the plant's own shareholder, is also one of its top ten suppliers.

steps.title: Finished cells go to US buyers
steps.text: 27 rows of cells went to the US, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026. The named buyers: EVE Energy North America 7, Briggs & Stratton 5 (two records), TTI Consumer Power Tools 2, and one each for Milwaukee Tool, Stanley Black & Decker, Energizer, ProTechnologies, ABM Tucker GA and a freight forwarder. Seven rows name no buyer. Most are rechargeable 21700 or 18650 cells (HS 8507.60); Energizer's and ProTechnologies' are non-rechargeable CR123A cells. After June 2026 every dated row lists Singapore, Yantian (China) or Pusan as the departure port, not Penang.

steps.title: A second plant, same shape: Linergy Power
steps.text: Linergy Power in Selangor was registered in Dec 2024. Until June 2026 it was 100% owned by Ampace Technology (Hong Kong), whose Xiamen parent is 59.5% owned by CATL. In June 2026 Japan's TDK bought all of it for US$241m through ATL's Singapore arm, so the Aug–Sep 2026 US rows were shipped under TDK ownership. Sayari's registry data still shows the old Ampace chain. It took 17 rows of artificial graphite from Zhongke Shinzoom and Shanshan, and shipped 17 rows of cells and battery systems to the US: Eaton 6, Ampace itself 6, Milwaukee Tool 3, Stanley Black & Decker 1 and Techtronic Product Development 1.

detected.text: Ownership: plant ← EVE Asia (Hong Kong) ← 100% EVE Energy Co., Ltd., with two directors shared between the plant and EVE Asia.
59 rows of battery-grade graphite into the plant from seven named suppliers, Apr 2025 to Apr 2026, including BTR's Indonesian plant from Case 1.
27 rows of cells from the plant to the US, with ten named buyer records, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026.
The parent carries a Section 1260H flag, confirmed by the DoD's 8 June 2026 list.
Linergy Power repeats the pattern: Zhongke and Shanshan graphite in, cells to Eaton, Milwaukee Tool and others out.
From filings, not Sayari: EVE Malaysia is 100% EVE (through EVE Asia); CATL holds 59.5% of Xiamen Ampace; TDK (Japan) bought 100% of Linergy Power in June 2026.

suggested.text: The Malaysian shareholder record and the Hong Kong registry company are the same EVE Asia (name, building and directors match).
HS 2842.90 imports from Hunan Yuneng, Changyuan Lico and Easpring are cathode powder. The HS code and names fit, but we didn't read the product text.

Since June 2026, cells under EVE Malaysia's name have left from Singapore, Yantian and Pusan. That could be transshipment, or cells loaded outside Malaysia; the data doesn't say which, and it warrants due diligence.
The 'Pinang' port on six EVE North America rows is probably Penang, Malaysia, not Indonesia as Sayari geocodes it.

red_flags.flag: Chinese parent ownership of the transit plant
red_flags.note: Registry chain to EVE Energy (100% of the HK holding company) plus shared directors.

red_flags.flag: Same HS imported from China and exported to the US
red_flags.note: Not this pattern: graphite (HS 3801) goes in and cells (HS 8507.60) come out. Real manufacturing happens in Malaysia.

red_flags.flag: Recent incorporation vs. first export date
red_flags.note: EVE Malaysia was formed Aug 2022 and made its first US shipment Oct 2025, normal for a new factory. Linergy took 11 months (Dec 2024 to Nov 2025).

red_flags.flag: Volume spike after a policy date
red_flags.note: No spike. One row on 19 Jun 2026, after the 8 Jun listing, still left from 'Pinang' (Penang). From July 2026 the US rows depart Singapore, Yantian or Pusan instead.

red_flags.flag: Shared address or officer with a flagged entity
red_flags.note: Directors shared with EVE Asia; one gives the address of the 1260H-listed parent.
Three plant records (one typed as a person), two EVE Asia records, two Briggs, Eaton and Milwaukee records each.
The plant has a Sheffield Hallam 'origin direct' flag via its suppliers. This is context, not a finding.

caveats: Making cells in Malaysia from Chinese materials is legal and common. Nothing here shows wrongdoing by any company named.
Buyers are named because they appear in customs records. That says nothing about their compliance, or whether they claim any US tax credit.

PFE rules work differently for cells and for anode material. For a US company claiming §45X on a product it makes, a bought-in cell counts as one input, and what matters is who made the cell. The anode material is an input of the cell maker, one step further back. We give no view on how the rules apply to any company here.
Trade data can't tie a given cell to a given graphite shipment.
The 1260H listing (8 June 2026) came after most of the trade shown here.
HS 2842.90 is read as cathode powder from the code and supplier names only.
Ownership percentages come from company filings, not Sayari. EVE's interim report shows EVE Malaysia at 100%, and CATL's Mar 2026 announcement shows CATL holding 59.5% of Xiamen Ampace.
Departure ports such as 'Pinang' and 'Hongkong' appear with mismatched countries in some rows. Treat the route details with care.

entities.name: EVE Energy Malaysia Sdn Bhd
entities.summary: EVE Energy's first plant outside China, in Kulim, Kedah. Registered 30 Aug 2022; first cell Feb 2025; 680 million cylindrical cells a year. It received 59 rows of anode graphite (HS 3801) from seven named suppliers, Apr 2025 to Apr 2026, and 27 rows of cells went to the US, Oct 2025 to Sep 2026. Its shareholder is EVE Asia (Hong Kong), which EVE Energy owns 100%.

params.query: 45X prohibited foreign entity specified foreign entity 1260H list foreign-influenced entity 25% battery cells components material assistance cost ratio threshold battery components

calls.question: How do the PFE rules treat a cell from a 1260H-linked maker, compared with anode material?
calls.result_summary: IRS Notice 2026-15 quotes §7701(a)(51): a 'specified foreign entity' includes an entity identified under Section 1260H. Law-firm summaries: a 'foreign-influenced entity' includes one where a single specified foreign entity owns more than 25%. For §45X, the material-assistance cost ratio compares direct material costs not made by a PFE with all direct material costs; the required non-PFE share for battery components is 60% for components sold in 2026, rising to 85% by 2030 (critical minerals 0% in 2026, 25% in 2030). IRS safe-harbor tables are due by 31 Dec 2026.
calls.interpretation: Cells and anode material sit at different points in the test. A US company buying finished cells counts the cell as one input, and what matters is who made the cell. Anode material is an input of the cell maker. We give no view on how the rules apply to any company here.
